insights.title: Your kidney function has fallen to stage G5
insights.found: On 22 Aug 2026 your eGFR was 6.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 and creatinine 10.85 mg/dL, flagged by the lab as critical. On 7 Apr 2026 they were 19.9 and 4.13.
insights.why: An eGFR below 15 is stage G5, the most advanced stage of chronic kidney disease, and the fall since May is large.
insights.means: At this level of kidney function, planning for kidney replacement (dialysis or a transplant) is part of care. Guidelines base decisions on the trend of results, not one value, and yours has moved quickly.
insights.do: Talk to your kidney team now about your 22 Aug 2026 results and the plan for dialysis or a transplant.
insights.expected: A clear plan made early avoids decisions in an emergency.
insights.helps: Shows where your kidneys stand today.

insights.title: Your gene test found a COL4A5 change that fits X-linked Alport syndrome
insights.found: Whole-exome sequencing found a hemizygous COL4A5 change, c.3143G>A p.Gly1048Glu, reported as a variant of uncertain significance with a high predicted-damage score (REVEL 0.96).
insights.why: COL4A5 makes a collagen of the kidney filter; glycine changes in it are the most common cause of X-linked Alport syndrome in men.
insights.means: In men with X-linked Alport syndrome, kidney failure often comes in the twenties, and the same change tends to behave alike within a family. The lab has not yet classed this change as disease-causing, so its formal label may change as evidence builds.
insights.do: Ask your doctor whether the variant can be reclassified, for example with testing of your mother or kidney tissue findings.
insights.expected: A confirmed cause guides treatment, family testing and transplant planning.
insights.helps: Explains why your kidneys are affected.

insights.title: Kidney-protecting medicines are the standard of care in Alport syndrome
insights.why: International guidelines name early renin-angiotensin system blockade (ACE inhibitor or ARB) as standard care in COL4A3/4/5 disease, with SGLT2 inhibitors as a possible add-on in adults.
insights.means: In advanced kidney disease these medicines still lower the risk of kidney failure, but they can raise potassium, which is already high for you. Whether and how to use them at your stage is your kidney team's decision.
insights.do: Ask your doctor which medicines you take now, and whether kidney-protecting treatment fits your stage.
insights.expected: A complete medicine list lets every check see what you take.

insights.title: Your haemoglobin is low
insights.found: Haemoglobin 10.4 g/dL on 22 Aug 2026 (9.4 on 7 Apr 2026), with red cell distribution width 15.0%, above the lab's range.
insights.why: It is below the healthy range for men. Anaemia is common when kidney function is this low.
insights.means: Guidelines ask for correctable causes such as low iron to be found and treated first; medicines that stimulate red cells come after that.
insights.do: Ask your doctor about iron studies (ferritin and transferrin saturation).
insights.expected: Treating the cause can lift energy and protect the heart.

insights.title: Your potassium has been above the lab's range
insights.found: Potassium 5.2 mmol/L on 22 Aug 2026 and 6.0 on 7 Apr 2026.
insights.why: The kidneys keep potassium in balance; at your stage they cannot fully do so.
insights.means: High potassium can affect heart rhythm, and some kidney medicines raise it further. It is watched closely in advanced kidney disease.
insights.do: Ask your kidney team about your potassium and whether diet or medicine changes are needed.
insights.expected: Keeping potassium in range keeps the heart safe.

insights.title: Your family may want testing
insights.found: X-linked Alport syndrome passes through the X chromosome.
insights.why: Mothers and sisters can carry the change; guidelines advise caution before relatives who carry it donate a kidney.
insights.means: Relatives who carry a COL4A variant should be considered for living kidney donation only as a last resort, because of their own kidney risk.
insights.do: Ask your doctor about genetic counselling and testing for your mother and siblings.
insights.expected: Family testing protects relatives and guides any living-donor transplant.

insights.title: Alport syndrome can affect hearing and eyes
insights.found: Your record has no hearing or eye examination.
insights.why: Within a family, the same COL4A5 change behaves consistently for hearing loss and eye changes (lenticonus).
insights.means: Hearing and eye checks are part of Alport care and can support the diagnosis.
insights.do: Ask for a hearing test and an eye examination.
insights.expected: Early hearing support makes daily life easier.

insights.title: Bone and mineral tests are recommended at your stage
insights.found: Calcium was 2.15 mmol/L on 22 Aug 2026; phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase are not on record.
insights.why: Guidance recommends monitoring calcium, phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase in kidney disease stage G5.
insights.means: Kidney failure changes how the body handles minerals, which affects bones and blood vessels.
insights.do: Ask for phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase at your next blood test.
insights.expected: Catches mineral changes before they affect bones.

insights.title: Your urate was just above the definition of high urate
insights.found: Serum urate 7.1 mg/dL on 22 Aug 2026 (5.9 on 7 Apr 2026).
insights.why: Our check flags urate above the boundary for high urate in men.
insights.means: Urate often rises when kidney function falls; without symptoms it is usually watched rather than treated.
insights.do: Mention it to your doctor with your kidney results.
insights.expected: Your doctor reads it with the rest of your kidney picture.

ask.a: On 22 Aug 2026 your eGFR was 6.2 and creatinine 10.85, which is stage G5, the most advanced stage. In May your eGFR was 19.9, so it has fallen quickly. Planning for dialysis or a transplant is part of care at this stage; talk to your kidney team now.

An inherited condition of a collagen in the kidney filter. Your gene test found a COL4A5 change that fits X-linked Alport syndrome in men. It is currently labelled a variant of uncertain significance, with a high predicted-damage score, so its formal label may change.
That is your kidney team's decision. With an eGFR of 6.2, planning for dialysis or a transplant is part of care. Ask them about timing and options, including a transplant.

X-linked Alport syndrome passes through the X chromosome, so your mother and sisters may carry it. Guidelines advise that relatives who carry the change donate a kidney only as a last resort. Genetic counselling is the right first step.
Your haemoglobin was 10.4 g/dL on 22 Aug 2026. Anaemia is common when kidney function is this low. Iron studies come first, because a correctable cause should be treated before other medicines.
It was 5.2 on 22 Aug 2026 and 6.0 on 7 Apr 2026, above the lab's range. High potassium can affect heart rhythm, so your kidney team watches it closely. Do not change diet or medicines without them.

ask.q: Which medicines help in Alport syndrome?
ask.a: Guidelines name early ACE inhibitor or ARB treatment as standard care, with SGLT2 inhibitors as a possible add-on in adults. At your stage they can raise potassium, so whether they fit is your kidney team's call. Your record lists no medicines.

ask.q: Will it affect my hearing or eyes?
ask.a: Alport syndrome can affect hearing and the eyes. Your record has no hearing or eye examination yet; both are worth doing.
Repeat kidney function and potassium; phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase; iron studies; urine albumin; a hearing test and an eye examination.

glossary: Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
A waste product from muscle, cleared by the kidneys; used to estimate kidney function.
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio: how much protein (albumin) leaks into the urine.
A blood salt needed for nerves, muscles and heart rhythm; the kidneys keep it in balance.
The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
Uric acid in the blood. High levels can form crystals in joints (gout).

genes.function: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen.
PPIase that catalyzes the cis-trans isomerization of proline imidic peptide bonds in oligopeptides and may therefore assist protein folding.

Metabolic-stress sensing protein kinase that phosphorylates the alpha subunit of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 (EIF2S1/eIF-2-alpha) in response to various stress, such as unfolded protein response (UPR).
Deacetylates a wide range of non-histone substrates.
Electrogenic Na(+)-coupled sugar symporter that actively transports D-glucose at the plasma membrane, with a Na(+) to sugar coupling ratio of 1:1.
Receptor for both mineralocorticoids (MC) such as aldosterone and glucocorticoids (GC) such as corticosterone or cortisol.
Receptor for angiotensin II, a vasoconstricting peptide, which acts as a key regulator of blood pressure and sodium retention by the kidney.

F12.statement: A national nephrology society commentary on KDIGO 2017 suggests monitoring calcium, phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase in adults with CKD G4 and recommends it in G5. It advises against this monitoring in G3.
F12.limitations: Commentary relied on KDIGO evidence summaries and did not replicate the systematic reviews. It addresses CKD-MBD only, not the full CKD evaluation.

F1.statement: KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD guidance covers adults with CKD G3a-G5 and dialysis. It emphasises basing treatment on trends in laboratory values rather than a single abnormal result, and avoiding hypercalcaemia when treating secondary hyperparathyroidism.
F1.limitations: The synopsis abstract does not list specific testing frequencies or targets.
F1.population: Adults with CKD G3a-G5 and on dialysis

F10.statement: The ERKNet/ERA/ESPN 2024 guideline recommends that relatives carrying heterozygous COL4A3/4/5 variants be considered for living kidney donation only as a last resort. This is relevant because potential living donors in this maternal-line X-linked family may be heterozygous carriers.
F10.limitations: Only the abstract is available. It does not give the strength or grade of the recommendation, donor eligibility criteria, or any guidance on timing of dialysis or pre-emptive transplantation.
F10.population: Individuals with pathogenic COL4A3/4/5 variants and their relatives being considered as living kidney donors

F9.statement: Guidelines advise caution with living-related donation from relatives carrying COL4A variants. The 2024 guideline says heterozygous relatives should be considered only as a last resort. The 2013 guideline discourages affected mothers of X-linked males from donating because of their own risk of kidney failure.
F9.limitations: Abstract-level statements; criteria for 'last possible resource' are not detailed.
F9.population: Relatives (especially mothers) of individuals with X-linked or other COL4A3/4/5 disease

F8.statement: Guidelines universally use serum ferritin to define iron deficiency, and about half add TSAT. Across conditions, the systematic review of guidelines concludes that a ferritin cut-off of 100 μg/L and a TSAT of 20% should be considered in most conditions.

F8.population: Adults across multiple indications, including CKD (29 guidelines, 2004-2014)

F2.statement: Within families, the phenotype of an individual COL4A5 mutation was very consistent for deafness, lenticonus and timing of ESRF onset. Glycine substitutions were the most common mutation class.
F2.limitations: The abstract gives no quantitative measure of intrafamilial concordance. Relatives' genotypes are unknown for this patient.
F2.population: Males with X-linked Alport syndrome in the meta-analysis.

F3.statement: In a Korean multicentre cohort of 130 males with XLAS, about 60% developed kidney failure, at a median age of 25.0 years. Truncating variants had worse kidney survival than non-truncating variants (HR 2.8). Sensorineural hearing loss occurred in 65.1% of males, and hearing survival was much worse with truncating than non-truncating variants (HR 5.1).
F3.limitations: This is a retrospective study with an East Asian cohort. The median age is not broken down for glycine missense variants specifically in the abstract. Ocular outcomes are not reported.

F5.statement: In an individual-participant meta-analysis of 18 RCTs in advanced CKD (baseline eGFR <30), starting an ACEi or ARB lowered the risk of KFRT but not death. Patient-level hyperkalaemia and AKI data were not available.
